mainTopic: Oaths and splitting the loss in the borrowed-or-rented cow case, unresolved questions about mixing borrowing and renting, and when a borrower's responsibility begins during delivery
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case. A שואל admits part of the owner's claim but says he doesn't know about the rest, so he cannot swear and must pay. Next comes a case from the משנה: the owner says the borrowed cow died and the renter says the rented one died. The משנה rules that the renter swears and is exempt. The גמרא asks where that oath comes from, and עולא answers that it comes through גלגול: it is attached to the oath that the cow died naturally. When neither side knows which cow died, they split the loss, following סומכוס. רבי אבא בר ממל then asks a chain of questions about a cow that is borrowed and rented back to back, some periods with the owner working for him and some without, and all of them end in תיקו. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a borrower is responsible for a cow that dies on the way only if he asked for, or agreed to, the messenger who brought it. The same rule applies when the cow is returned.

steps.title: The borrower who cannot swear must pay
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier case. The borrower denies one cow, admits the borrowed one died, and does not know about the other cow. Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The borrower says: about one cow, this never happened. About another, yes, the borrowed one died. About the other one, I don't know whether the rented one died and the living one is the borrowed one, or the borrowed one died and the living one is the rented one. Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier case about a שואל who admits part of the owner's claim but honestly does not know the facts about another part. The ruling is that because he cannot swear, he must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the borrower admits part of the claim, he would normally have to take a שבועה to be free from the rest. He openly says 'I don't know,' so he cannot swear about that part. The rule מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם means he pays instead of swearing.

keyTerms.meaning: A borrower, someone who uses an item for free. Here it does not mean 'asks.'
It never happened; a complete denial
Since he cannot swear, he pays

steps.whatToRemember: When someone must take an oath but cannot, because he admits he doesn't know the facts, he pays: מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם.
steps.confusionAlert: Here שׁוֹאֵל means 'the borrower,' not 'he asks.' Reading it as a question will make the whole line confusing.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹאֵל: חֲדָא – לֹא הָיוּ דְבָרִים מֵעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: The borrower says: about one, this never happened.
And about one: yes, the borrowed one died,
and about the other one, I don't know
whether the rented one died and the one still alive is the borrowed one,
or the borrowed one died and the one still alive is the rented one,
for since he cannot swear, he pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a case that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A bailee who must swear but admits he does not know the facts cannot swear, so he pays.

steps.title: The משנה: owner says borrowed, renter says rented
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. When the owner says the borrowed cow died and the renter says the rented cow died, the renter swears and is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one says it was the borrowed one, and that one says it was the rented one. The renter swears that the rented one died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The renter had one cow rented and one borrowed, and one cow died. If the borrowed cow died, he must pay, because a borrower pays even for accidents. If the rented cow died naturally, a שוכר is exempt. The owner and the renter each claim to be sure, and the משנה lets the renter swear and go free.

keyTerms.meaning: A renter, who pays to use the item

phrases.english: This one says: it was the borrowed one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the owner and 'that one' is the person who rented and borrowed the cows.

phrases.english: and that one says: it was the rented one,
the renter swears that the rented one died.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר שְׁאוּלָה, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר שְׂכוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When each side is sure, the renter swears that the rented cow died and is exempt.

steps.title: Why should the renter swear at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there is an oath here. The renter did not admit to any part of the owner's claim, so the rule of מודה במקצת does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? What the owner claimed, the renter did not admit to him. And what the renter admitted to, the owner did not claim from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the renter takes an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath from the תורה comes when the defendant admits part of the very thing being claimed (מודה במקצת). Here the owner claims the borrowed cow died, and the renter admits nothing about that. The renter only says the rented cow died, which the owner never claimed. So there seems to be no basis for an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: One who admits part of a claim and must swear about the rest

phrases.english: But why?
What he claimed from him, he did not admit to him,
and what he admitted to him, he did not claim from him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? מַה שֶּׁטְּעָנוֹ – לֹא הוֹדָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the renter swears.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oath requires partial admission of the actual claim. Here the claim and the admission do not overlap at all.

steps.title: עולא: the oath comes through גלגול
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the oath here is not a regular מודה במקצת oath. It is attached, or 'rolled on,' to another oath the renter already owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is by means of 'rolling over' an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge. The renter's oath comes through גלגול שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גלגול means that once a person is required to swear about one thing, the other side can add more claims to that oath. So the renter does not need a partial admission for this claim. The next step explains which oath it is attached to.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
Attaching extra claims to an oath someone already has to take

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is by means of rolling over.
phrases.notes: He means the oath is 'rolled on' to another oath the renter already has to take.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different source for the oath.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath must be a מודה במקצת oath, which needs partial admission.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath comes from גלגול, so no partial admission is needed.

steps.title: How the גלגול works here
steps.stepSummary: The owner can demand that the renter swear the cow died naturally. Since the renter swears that anyway, the owner adds that it was the rented cow that died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner said to him: 'Swear to me, at any rate, that it died in its normal way.' And since he swears that it died naturally, he also swears that the rented one died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains עולא's answer and shows which oath the new claim is attached to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whichever cow it was, the renter owes an oath that it died naturally and not through his negligence. Once he is already swearing that oath, the owner uses גלגול to add the claim 'swear it was the rented one.' This is why the משנה says the renter swears that the rented cow died.

keyTerms.meaning: It died in its normal way, naturally, without negligence
Since; because he is already doing one thing

steps.whatToRemember: The renter's oath does not come from מודה במקצת. It is rolled on (גלגול) to his oath that the cow died naturally.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that גלגול can create an oath even when a claim alone would never require one.

phrases.english: Where the owner said to him:
Swear to me, at any rate,
phrases.notes: He means: whichever cow it was, you owe me at least this oath.

phrases.english: that it died in its normal way,
and since he swears that it died in its normal way,
he also swears that the rented one died.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִישְׁתְּבַע לִי אֵיזוֹ מִיהַת דִּכְדַרְכָּהּ מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how עולא's גלגול works in this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the base oath that the claim is attached to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no oath the claim could be attached to.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath that the cow died naturally serves as the base, and the claim about which cow died is rolled onto it.

steps.title: Quoting the last case of the משנה: neither side knows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last line of the משנה, where both the owner and the renter say 'I don't know' which cow died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: this one says 'I don't know,' and that one says 'I don't know,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה so it can explain it. This line sets up the question about whose opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case neither the owner nor the renter knows which cow died, the borrowed one or the rented one. The משנה rules that they split the loss. The word כו׳ ('etc.') points to the rest of the משנה line, which the גמרא does not repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'etc.': the rest of the quoted line is left out

phrases.english: This one says: I do not know
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the owner and 'that one' is the renter. Neither knows which cow died.

phrases.english: and that one says, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line in the משנה is: 'I do not know', so they split it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ וְזֶה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the oath case (steps 2-5) to the next case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When neither party knows which cow died, they divide the loss.

steps.title: The split ruling follows סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the 'split it' ruling follows and answers: סומכוס, who says money in doubt is divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is סומכוס, who says: money whose ownership is in doubt is divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who holds this way and answers right away: it is סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the one who wants to take money must bring proof (המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה). If that rule applied, the renter would not pay without proof. Splitting the loss fits סומכוס, who holds that when ownership of money is in doubt, the two sides divide it.

keyTerms.meaning: סומכוס, a תנא with his own view on money in doubt
money whose ownership is in doubt

steps.whatToRemember: The 'split it' ruling for 'I don't know / I don't know' follows סומכוס: money in doubt is divided.

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is סומכוס,
who says: money lying in doubt, they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose opinion the quoted משנה line follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the parties split the loss here?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סומכוס, who rules that money in doubt is divided.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This line of the משנה follows סומכוס, not the usual rule that the claimant must bring proof.

steps.title: Borrowed with the owner, then rented without the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל asks: someone borrowed a cow while the owner was working for him, then rented it without the owner. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל asked: if he borrowed it with the owner, and rented it without the owner, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי אבא בר ממל describes a case where one person first borrows a cow and then rents the same cow, and asks what the law is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Borrowing 'with the owner' (שאלה בבעלים) means the owner was also working for the borrower at the time, and in that case the borrower is not liable. The renting happened without the owner, which normally means the renter is liable for theft and loss. The question is which rule wins when the two periods run back to back.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked a question that has no clear answer yet
he borrowed it while the owner was working for him
he rented it without the owner working for him

steps.confusionAlert: 'With the owner' does not mean the owner was standing next to the cow. It means the owner himself was working for the borrower when the borrowing began.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel asked:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאָלָהּ בִּבְעָלִים, שְׂכָרָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּבְעָלִים, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: He borrowed it with its owner, then rented it without its owner: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how back-to-back borrowing and renting of one cow work together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the renter liable for the rental period when the borrowing before it was 'with the owner'?

steps.title: Two sides: separate deals, or is renting tied to borrowing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides. Either borrowing and renting are separate, or the renting is pulled along by the borrowing because both carry liability for theft and loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say the borrowing stands alone and the renting stands alone? Or perhaps renting is connected to borrowing, since a renter is also liable for theft and loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two ways to look at רבי אבא בר ממל's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the two are separate deals, so the rental period is judged by itself. The owner was not working for him then, so the renter is liable. Side two: renting is close to borrowing, since both are liable for theft and loss. So the renting may be a continuation of the borrowing, and the borrowing was 'with the owner', which means no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: it stands by itself, as a separate deal
they are connected to each other

steps.whyThisMatters: The question is whether two back-to-back deals on one object are judged separately or as one continuing deal. The answer decides whether the 'with the owner' exemption carries over.

phrases.english: Do we say the borrowing stands by itself
and the renting stands by itself,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא שְׂכִירוּת בִּשְׁאֵלָה מֵישָׁךְ שָׁיְיכִי,
phrases.english: or perhaps renting is connected to borrowing,
since he is liable for theft and loss?
phrases.notes: A renter, like a borrower, pays if the animal is stolen or lost. That shared liability is what links them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two possible sides of the question in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are borrowing and renting separate deals, or is the renting an extension of the borrowing?

steps.title: The reverse case: rented with the owner, then borrowed without
steps.stepSummary: Suppose renting is connected to borrowing. What about the reverse case: rented with the owner, then borrowed without the owner?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say renting is connected to borrowing, then if he rented it with the owner and borrowed it without the owner, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a follow-up question. Even if the first question is answered 'connected', the reverse order is still unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אם תמצא לומר' means: suppose the answer to the first question is that the renting is tied to the borrowing. Even so, we still need to know about the opposite order. If he rented first with the owner, then borrowed without the owner, is the later borrowing also pulled along by the earlier renting?

keyTerms.meaning: if you will say (suppose the first question is answered this way)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order flip. In step 8 the borrowing came first, with the owner. Here the renting comes first, with the owner, and the borrowing comes second, without him.

phrases.english: If you will say
renting is connected to borrowing,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכָרָהּ בִּבְעָלִים שְׁאָלָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּבְעָלִים, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: if he rented it with its owner and borrowed it without its owner, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up that builds on one possible answer to step 9 and asks about the reverse order.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If renting after borrowing is tied to the borrowing, is borrowing after renting also tied to the renting?

steps.title: Is borrowing connected to an earlier renting?
steps.stepSummary: In the reverse case (rented with the owner, then borrowed without the owner), the גמרא lays out both sides: either borrowing is not connected to renting at all, or a partial connection counts as a full one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say borrowing is surely not connected to renting? Or, since it is partly connected, is it treated as if fully connected?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible sides of the question it just asked in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower is liable for more than a renter, because he also pays for accidents (אונסין). So borrowing is not simply a 'continuation' of renting. But a borrower and a renter both pay for theft and loss, so they overlap partly. The question is whether that partial overlap is enough to let the borrowing be pulled along by the earlier renting, so the owner-was-with-him exemption would still apply.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 9 renting was pulled along by borrowing. Here it is the other way around. Borrowing is the stricter one, so it is harder to say it is 'swallowed' by renting.

phrases.english: Borrowing, in relation to renting,
phrases.notes: He means the later borrowing compared to the earlier renting of the same cow.

phrases.english: is certainly not connected,
or perhaps, since it is partly connected,
it is treated as if it were fully connected?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁאֵלָה בִּשְׂכִירוּת וַדַּאי לָא שָׁיְיכָא, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the reverse-case question from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a partial overlap in liability is enough to tie a later borrowing to an earlier renting.

steps.title: Borrowed, then rented, then borrowed again
steps.stepSummary: Assuming partial connection does not count, the גמרא asks a new case: borrowed with the owner, rented without the owner, then borrowed again. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we do not treat a partial connection as a full one, then: he borrowed the cow with the owner, rented it without the owner, and then borrowed it again. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a new question on top of the last one: the cow goes from borrowing to renting and back to borrowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If borrowing cannot be pulled along by renting, the last borrowing cannot lean on the renting in the middle. But maybe it can lean on the first borrowing, which was with the owner. The question is whether the first and last borrowings join together across the gap.

keyTerms.meaning: if you will say (if the answer to the last question is this)
with the owner working for him

phrases.english: If you will say
phrases.notes: He means: if the answer to step 11 is 'no, partly connected is not fully connected.'

phrases.english: we do not say that since it is partly connected
it is treated as if fully connected,
he borrowed it with the owner,
and rented it without the owner,
and then borrowed it again; what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the 'not connected' side of step 11 and asks a further case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a third-period borrowing joins up with a first-period borrowing that was done with the owner.

steps.title: Does the borrowing come back, or does the renting cut it off?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides: either the borrowing returns to its place, or the renting in the middle breaks the link.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the borrowing come back to its place? Or perhaps the renting cut it off in between?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two sides of the question it just asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the last borrowing is really a continuation of the first borrowing, so it is still covered by the owner-was-with-him exemption. Side two: the renting in the middle is a break, so the last borrowing stands alone without the owner, and the borrower is fully liable.

phrases.english: Does the borrowing come back to its place,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אִפְּסִיקָא לַהּ שְׂכִירוּת בֵּינֵי וּבֵינֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps the renting cut it off in between?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the step 12 question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a middle period of renting breaks the link between two periods of borrowing.

steps.title: Rented, then borrowed, then rented again
steps.stepSummary: The mirror case: rented with the owner, then borrowed, then rented again. Does the renting come back, or does the borrowing in the middle cut it off?
steps.simpleTranslation: He rented it with the owner, then borrowed it, then rented it again. What is the law? Do we say the renting comes back to its place, or perhaps the borrowing cut it off in between?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question with the order flipped, and the section ends with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first and last periods are renting, and borrowing sits in the middle. The question is whether the last renting joins the first renting (done with the owner) and keeps the exemption, or whether the borrowing in the middle breaks the chain.
steps.whatToRemember: All these questions ask one thing: when the cow moves between borrowing and renting, does the first period (done with the owner) reach forward to cover later periods? The גמרא leaves them unanswered here.

phrases.english: He rented it with the owner,
and borrowed it, and then rented it again; what is the law?
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say it, but the later periods are without the owner, like in the earlier cases.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן אָתְיָא לַהּ שְׂכִירוּת לְדוּכְתַּהּ
phrases.english: Do we say the renting comes back to its place,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אִפְּסִיקָא לַהּ שְׁאֵלָה בֵּינֵי וּבֵינֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps the borrowing cut it off in between?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂכָרָהּ בִּבְעָלִים וּשְׁאָלָהּ וְחָזַר וּשְׂכָרָהּ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of steps 12-13, with renting on the outside and borrowing in the middle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a middle period of borrowing breaks the link between two periods of renting.

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the whole series of questions about borrowing and renting with תיקו. They are left without an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot settle the questions it just asked, so it leaves them open with the word תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8–14 asked whether borrowing and renting can link up, and what happens when one interrupts the other. No source decides these cases, so they stay as open questions. תיקו is not a ruling that the answer is unknowable; it simply means the matter remains undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: All the questions about linking borrowing with renting, and about a break in the middle, end as תיקו. None of them gets an answer.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].
phrases.notes: This closes all the questions from the last several steps, not just the final one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chain of questions in steps 8–14 without resolving them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about linking borrowing with renting remain unresolved.

steps.title: Lender sends the cow on his own: borrower is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If the lender sends the cow through any messenger without the שואל asking for it, and the cow dies on the way, the שואל is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone borrowed a cow. The lender sent it to him through the lender's own son, slave or agent, or through the borrower's son, slave or agent. The cow died on the way. The borrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It rules that when the lender sends the cow on his own initiative, the borrower is not responsible for a death on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the borrower never asked for the cow to be sent this way. So the borrowing has not started yet, and the risk is still the lender's. Notice that this holds even when the messenger belongs to the borrower, such as his own son or slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה.
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Even when the messenger is the borrower's own son or slave, the borrower is still פטור. What counts is that he did not ask for the cow to be sent.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who borrowed the cow
and [the lender] sent it to him by the hand of his son,
by the hand of his slave, by the hand of his agent,
or by the hand of the son, by the hand of the slave
or by the hand of the agent of the borrower,
and it died: [the borrower] is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹאֵל אֶת הַפָּרָה וְשִׁלְּחָהּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the lender sends the cow on his own initiative, the borrower is exempt if it dies on the way.

steps.title: Borrower asked for or agreed to the sending: borrower is liable
steps.stepSummary: The borrower is חייב for a death on the way in two cases: if he asked for the cow to be sent through a certain messenger, or if he agreed when the lender proposed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose the borrower said: send it to me through my son, slave or agent, or through your son, slave or agent. Or suppose the lender said: I am sending it to you through my son, slave or agent, or through your son, slave or agent, and the borrower answered: send it. Then the lender sent it and it died. In both cases the borrower is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. When the borrower himself requested or approved the messenger, he is responsible from the moment the messenger takes the cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What changed from the last step is the borrower's consent. Once he approves the messenger, that messenger stands in his place. So his responsibility as a שואל begins when the messenger receives the cow, even before it reaches his home.

keyTerms.meaning: Lender, the owner who lends the item
Send! The borrower's word of agreement

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a שואל's responsibility starts when the item reaches him or anyone he authorized to receive it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case: with the borrower's consent, the ruling flips from exempt to liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the borrower requested or approved the messenger, he is liable for a death on the way.

steps.title: The same rules apply when returning the cow
steps.stepSummary: The same rules work in reverse when the borrower sends the cow back to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same applies when he returns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that these rules also apply on the return trip, from borrower back to lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the borrower sends the cow back through a messenger the lender never approved. Then the borrower stays responsible until it reaches the lender. If the lender approved that messenger, the borrower's responsibility ends once the messenger takes the cow.
steps.whatToRemember: Whoever did not agree to the messenger is not affected by the handoff to him. On the way there, the risk stays with the lender; on the way back, it stays with the borrower.

phrases.english: And likewise at the time that he returns it.
phrases.notes: Now the roles flip: it is the lender's consent to the messenger that decides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rules of steps 16–17 to the return of the cow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The consent-based rules for sending the cow also apply when the borrower returns it.
